item.title: Ukraine's attacks on Russia are pushing Putin closer to negotiating table, Trump NATO ambassador says
item.description: Matt Whitaker says Ukrainian attacks inside Russia are pushing both sides closer to peace talks as Trump presses Putin and Zelenskyy to negotiate.
item.content:encoded:
Ukrainian attacks inside Russia are helping push Moscow and Kyiv closer to the negotiating table, U.S. Ambassador to NATO Matt Whitaker said on Saturday, as President Donald Trump continues pressing Russian President Vladimir Putin and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy to negotiate an end to the war.

Whitaker emphasized during "The Big Weekend Show" that it would take the cooperation of both adversaries to end the war, but said Ukraine "continuing to make strong attacks on Russia... is helping to, I think, bring the sides closer together."

The ambassador cautioned that Moscow and Kyiv still remain "a long way apart" on key issues, adding that the resolution would not come through hostilities.

UKRAINE STRIKES DEEP INTO RUSSIA’S ARCTIC GAS HEARTLAND AS TRUMP PUSHES PUTIN TOWARD PEACE

"This conflict is not going to be resolved on the battlefield. It's only going to [be resolved] through diplomacy and negotiation," he said.

"That's why President Trump and his team continue to talk to both sides to find any similarities between the positions to bring them together."

ZELENSKYY TO SEEK OFFRAMP FOR YEARS-LONG RUSSIA WAR IN UN SPEECH AFTER TRUMP REVEALS PEACE DEAL IS CLOSE

If Putin is unwilling to compromise, striking a deal will be "impossible," said Whitaker.

"But I think if there's a deal to be made, President Trump is a businessman, he's a dealmaker, and I think he'll make the deal."

Trump said Saturday that 25,000 people were killed last month and another 32,000 the month before in the war between Ukraine and Russia.

FINLAND'S STUBB CREDITS TRUMP FOR PUSHING UKRAINE PEACE TALKS WHILE DISMISSING RUSSIAN INVASION FEARS

"Last month, 25,000 people died in the Ukraine-Russia war, okay? Twenty-five thousand," Trump told reporters on the White House lawn.

"The month before that, 32,000 people died … mostly soldiers, 97% soldiers," he added. "But whether they're soldiers or civilians, think of it: 32,000. Two months ago, 33,000 people; this month, 25,000 people died. What a shame."

Russia alone has lost as many as 450,000 soldiers since invading Ukraine in 2022, according to the Center for Strategic & International Studies (CSIS).

item.title: Bass angler couldn't use LiveScope, so he followed whitetail deer to find the fish instead
item.description: Kaden Buchmann used deer sightings to gauge fishing pressure at Norfork Lake, going wire-to-wire without forward-facing sonar to win $71,317.
item.content:encoded:
What do you do when you can't use LiveScope to find the bass?

You ask the deer, obviously.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE FROM OUTKICK OUTDOORS

Kaden Buchmann went wire-to-wire to win the first Bassmaster Elite Qualifier of the season Friday at Norfork Lake in Arkansas, finishing the three-day tournament with 42 pounds, 7 ounces.

But the fun part is how the 22-year-old found some of those fish.

Forward-facing sonar was not allowed for the Norfork event, one of three Elite Qualifiers that will ultimately determine which 10 anglers earn invitations to the 2027 Bassmaster Elite Series. So Buchmann had to find another way to figure out where bass might be hiding — and, more importantly, where 130-plus other anglers hadn't already been.

His solution was to ask the locals. Well, the four-legged locals.

With so many boats working a relatively small reservoir, Buchmann started watching the shoreline for deer. If deer were hanging out close to the water, chances were pretty good another angler hadn't just come ripping through that pocket and scared them off.

"If I saw 15 deer in a pocket, I'd say, 'I'm getting bit here,'" Buchmann told Bassmaster.

And, somehow, it worked.

Buchmann spotted more than 30 deer during the opening day of competition — including a 9-point buck — and used their presence as a clue for finding areas that hadn't seen as much fishing pressure. He weighed 16 pounds, 7 ounces that day to take the tournament lead.

TREY MCKINNEY SAYS BASSMASTER VETERANS MADE HIM EARN THEIR RESPECT BEFORE HISTORIC AOY SEASON

Then he did it again.

On Day 2, Buchmann once again spent part of his morning looking for deer and said he caught two quality bass in a pocket where he had spotted them.

"We can't use (forward-facing sonar) this week, so you just have to fish where you think they're gonna be," he told Bassmaster.

Simple enough. But not easy.

To be clear, Buchmann did a whole lot more than follow deer around Norfork Lake.

Bassmaster credited his speed, mental toughness and ability to stay away from other competitors as major factors in the win. He covered enormous stretches of the lake, kept his trolling motor running high and targeted everything from docks to shaded shoreline with a topwater bait and skipping jig. On the final day alone, he said four of the fish he weighed came from places he had never previously fished.

"I fished the whole lake," Buchmann said after the win. "I fished from about 3 miles from Missouri, all the way down to a pocket by the Norfork Dam."

It all added up to a wire-to-wire victory.

Buchmann opened with 16-7, added 14 pounds on Day 2 and survived a tougher final round with another 12 pounds. His 42-7 total beat runner-up Cody Stahl by 1 pound, 14 ounces and earned Buchmann $71,317 along with an invitation to compete in the 2027 Bassmaster Classic at Lake Hartwell.

There are still two Elite Qualifiers remaining before the 10 Bassmaster Elite Series invitations are handed out, so Buchmann has plenty of work left to do.

But now that his deer-scouting secret is out, don’t be surprised if there are a few more anglers watching the shoreline next time.

item.title: Why the New Orleans Saints can cover the spread against the Las Vegas Raiders in NFL Week 3
item.description: The Las Vegas Raiders face the New Orleans Saints in Week 3 as both teams look to prove their early-season success wasn't a fluke against each other.
item.content:encoded:
Each NFL season has its own story and uniqueness. Discovering it is part of the fun, but it can also be a point of contention when you’re a sports bettor. You don’t have a ton of time to determine who is a good team and who is bad. You have to constantly evaluate and change your opinions on things. I’ve already changed my opinion on both of these teams – the Raiders and the Saints, and now they face each other in Week 3.

The Las Vegas Raiders cost me some money last week, or maybe I should say the Chargers cost me money once again. After backing them in Week 1, I took the Chargers to beat them in Week 2 and cover the spread. The Raiders looked like a fairly well-oiled machine against Los Angeles, getting three touchdown passes from Kirk Cousins on 19-for-29 passing. Part of the key for the Raiders will be keeping Cousins upright, and he was only sacked twice.

The other key to the Raiders' success is getting Ashton Jeanty to effectively run the ball. What I liked about the Raiders game is that despite him not having a very good game, they stuck with it. Jeanty had just 48 yards on 21 attempts. He did haul in four of his seven targets, but added just 15 yards. Before we crown the Raiders as being elite, let’s realize that the Chargers were also part of their problem. Sure, some of this can be attributed to Las Vegas, but Los Angeles fumbling six times was also ridiculous.

The New Orleans Saints have put together some decent games to start their season. They almost came back and beat the Lions in Week 1 after bringing them to overtime. In the first two quarters of the season, the Saints scored zero total points. Since about the middle of the third quarter of that game, they have scored 54 points. All of their touchdowns have come through the air as well, relying on Tyler Shough to lead the way.

If you want to get even more granular with the team, to see where the struggles and successes have been, let’s take a look at Week 2. The Saints have scored six total points in the first half of the two games. In the fourth quarter and overtime, they’ve scored 40 points. Maybe it is Shough taking too long to figure out opposing defenses. Maybe there is some other reason, but they are playing with fire by waiting until the last quarter to try and come back.

The Saints have played two rather difficult teams and now get to play at home. The Raiders had an easy game to open the season, and their second game wasn’t exactly a challenge considering how bad the Chargers look. Again, some of that was certainly self-inflicted, but I don’t want to take a ton away from the Raiders. I just don’t think this is a great situation for the Raiders. I don’t think their offense will be able to be quite as effective in this one. I like the Saints to win and cover the -3 spread.

item.title: Panthers favored at -2.5 over Browns as Bryce Young's offense faces Cleveland's home opener
item.description: Bryce Young has thrown six touchdown passes through two weeks, and now the Panthers face a Cleveland Browns team coming off a lightning-aided upset.
item.content:encoded:
You can go ahead and tell me I’m a glutton for punishment, and maybe I’m a fool, but there are some games that stood out to me this weekend, and both involved teams that hurt me last weekend. I’m not chasing any sort of win; I just feel like this one is the correct angle for the game. Today we start with two teams that both got back on track last weekend as the Panthers take on the Browns.

Lost in the mess that was Week 1 was how good the Panthers offense looked against the Chicago Bears. Of course, the main story was that the Panthers allowed 59 points, but they put up 37 of their own. Bryce Young looked solid in the contest with 361 yards, three touchdowns, and one interception. That’s a game typically good enough to beat most teams. His defense just gave him no help. Even the running game was performing well, but they had to somewhat abandon it.

Last week the team was dominant in a road victory over the Falcons. It wasn’t just an offensive victory; the defense adjusted and held Atlanta to just a field goal in the game. Before you anoint the defense completely back on track, just keep in mind that the Falcons turned the ball over three times. They had almost 100 yards more on the ground, meaning the Panthers have given up a many of yards through two games to opponents' rushing attacks. The offense with Young was still rolling. He threw for another three touchdowns in the game.

The Cleveland Browns broke the hearts of a lot of people last week. That’s nothing new for a franchise that seems to thrive on hurting people’s hearts. However, this time it was because the Browns took down the Buccaneers on the road in Week 2. That knocked out another 30% of the remaining Circa Survivor entries (including mine). But was this the Browns playing great, the Bucs playing bad, or both? It probably lies somewhere in between. Deshaun Watson played a strong game.

After a terrible Week 1, Watson went 24-for-30 through the air with two touchdown passes. He added 22 yards on the ground, which was a team high for the Browns. There also was an act of God that helped the Browns capture the victory. The Buccaneers were mounting a comeback and working the ball downfield when lightning struck. That suspended the game and took away any momentum that Tampa had. The Buccaneers' penalties after the play resumed cost the Bucs the game and put Cleveland at 1-1 after a terrible opener against Jacksonville.

Something is definitely wrong with Tampa Bay, but I don’t want to take too much away from Cleveland. Watson looked good for the first time in years. Still, I think the line is too low for the Panthers. I know they are playing their second straight road game, and it's a home opener for Cleveland, but the team is significantly better than the Browns. I also think their biggest weakness, the opposing running game, is not a strength of the Browns. Give me Carolina -2.5.

item.title: Jaxson Dart's girlfriend isn't letting the Giants quarterback's season-ending injury slow her down
item.description: Marissa Ayers shared an emotional TikTok video after Jaxson Dart's season-ending knee injury, vowing to stand by him through his road to recovery.
item.content:encoded:
Jaxson Dart, the New York Giants, and the quarterback's girlfriend Marissa Ayers all came out guns blazing to start the season. The second-year signal caller went 23 of 29 for 230 yards and three touchdowns in Week 1.

The Giants defeated the Dallas Cowboys and looked like a team that was preparing to take the next step. Ayers stepped her game up as well and received praise for her performance to start the season.

Then, just seven plays into the Week 2 game against the Los Angeles Rams, the Giants lost their starting quarterback. Dart went down with what turned out to be a season-ending knee injury.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Where do you go from there if you're the Giants? They've for the moment handed the offense over to veteran backup Jameis Winston.

Marissa Ayers isn't going to turn her up-and-coming WAG duties over to anyone else. While the season took a turn and there was no victory celebration in Week 2, she set the tone for the rest of the season prior to Week 3 kicking off.

"It has been an emotional few days. My sweet Jax," she wrote in the caption of a TikTok video. "Your unconditional love and drive for this sport will push you through this temporary pain being away from it. We now place full trust in God to wrap His arms around you to heal your body and lift your spirits."

Ayers continued, "The road to recovery begins, and I promise to keep you covered in so much love and prayer through it all. Jax you are the most determined and resilient person I know. You inspire me to show up for myself — my dreams and goals even when it’s difficult."

LEGENDARY AGENT LEIGH STEINBERG HAS SIMPLE ADVICE FOR GIANTS STAR JAXSON DART AFTER CRUSHING KNEE INJURY

We're a little more than halfway through this and if he wasn't injured, Dart just might be running straight through a brick wall. If there was any doubt about where she stood after participating in the NFL's girlfriend propaganda campaign, that's gone. She's built for the NFL.

"So I promise to remind you of that strength you have instilled in me every single day. There is not a doubt in my mind that you will come back even stronger than before," Ayers added.

"You can do everything you set your mind to — I’ve seen it firsthand, and I’ll be here to hold your hand each step of the way. I love you. @Darty"

That's how you make a name for yourself in this league. The talent is undeniable. It's not how you approach the game when things are going well. It's all about how you respond when you get knocked down.

Marissa Ayers popped right back to her feet, and she's going to help Jaxson Dart do the same. That's how you wake up one day and find yourself as the face of the league.

item.title: Bruce Campbell says Hollywood studios left ‘very sour’ taste after he was 'kicked out' of lead role
item.description: After a cancer diagnosis and decades in Hollywood, Bruce Campbell and wife Ida Gearon filmed "Ernie & Emma" entirely in their home state of Oregon.
item.content:encoded:
Bruce Campbell is taking a chainsaw to the Hollywood playbook.

The "Evil Dead" star is ditching the traditional studio system for "Ernie & Emma," his new independent film that puts him firmly in the driver's seat after decades of navigating Hollywood — and after one early studio experience left a bad taste.

"The first studio film I ever did, I got kicked out of the lead," Campbell told Fox News Digital. "The movie was re-edited, retitled and never came out. So, the taste in my mouth from studios is very sour."

KEVIN SORBO BLASTS HOLLYWOOD 'BLACKLISTING' OF CONSERVATIVES AS 'SEVENTH GRADE MEAN GIRLS' CULTURE

That experience stuck with the cult-favorite actor, who said he has long wanted to make a project without studio executives calling the shots.

"It was time to be unbridled in my life," Campbell said.

WATCH: BRUCE CAMPBELL SAYS HOLLYWOOD STUDIOS LEFT 'VERY SOUR' TASTE IN HIS MOUTH

The decision carries extra weight following Campbell's cancer diagnosis, which he disclosed in March. 

Campbell said earlier this month on "The Adam Carolla Show" podcast that doctors had given him an estimated five years to live, but he remains focused on treatment and continuing his work.

The actor wrote, directed, produced and stars in "Ernie & Emma," which he made independently with his wife and longtime partner, Ida Gearon.

For Campbell, the project represents a return to the kind of creative freedom he experienced early in his career with "The Evil Dead."

TAYLOR SHERIDAN TAKES SWIPE AT LOS ANGELES AFTER BUILDING TV EMPIRE FROM TEXAS

"The very first movie we did, ‘Evil Dead,’ was the only other movie I've ever done free and clear of the studio system," he said. "So, I liked the taste of it early on."

"I wanted to do something like this for a long time, and my wife finally said, ‘Quit talking about it. Let's do it. Let's pull the trigger. Let's make this movie," he recalled.

WATCH: ACTOR BRUCE CAMPBELL TOUTS MAKING FILM WITH WIFE: 'WE NEVER ARGUED ONCE'

'BLUE BLOODS' STAR JENNIFER ESPOSITO SAYS SHE WALKED AWAY FROM HOLLYWOOD AFTER YEARS OF REJECTION AND ‘ABUSE’

The actor has little interest in pretending creative control is easy to maintain when someone else is financing the production.

"Creative freedom is absolutely everything," Campbell said. "If you consider yourself an artiste, or you're in the arts, the only way that artists have to deal with people, outside of themselves, is to go look for money."

"Ernie & Emma" marks a dramatic departure from the horror and action roles that made Campbell a genre icon. 

The movie follows Ernie Tyler, a small-town pear salesman who embarks on a road trip through Pear Valley, Oregon, after his beloved wife, Emma, dies.

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

Emma leaves Ernie a detailed list of instructions for scattering her ashes, sending him on a journey through grief, love and the possibility of starting over.

Campbell and Gearon filmed the movie entirely in southern Oregon, turning their home state into the backdrop for the story — and their own lives into an unconventional production setup.

Gearon, a longtime costume designer, encouraged Campbell to keep the shoot close to home.

GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE

"She goes, ‘Bruce, we should shoot in Oregon. You should sleep in your own bed. You should [be having lunch] at the house,’" Campbell said. "And so, I did, and it was a very bizarre experience, but I'll never go back now."

"Best part of working with my wife was that, for once, we didn't argue," he said. "We argue a lot and when we made the movie we never argued once because we had a singular goal, singular vision."

After more than three decades together, Campbell said his relationship with Gearon has evolved into something deeper than romance.

"Boy, my wife, she is rock solid. She's a good human being from A to Z. I trust her," he said.

"The other day we said to each other, we've been together so long we're actually family now."

Campbell is taking "Ernie & Emma" on the road with a nationwide screening tour at Alamo Drafthouse locations, following earlier sold-out screenings at independent theaters.

item.title: Irish PM rejects antisemitism concerns in Ireland amid dramatic vote over boycotting Israel game
item.description: Irish Prime Minister Micheál Martin rejected antisemitism claims as Ireland's soccer players held a dramatic last-minute vote on playing against Israel.
item.content:encoded:
Irish Prime Minister Micheál Martin rejected claims that Ireland's sharp criticism of Israel has crossed into antisemitism as tensions flared around a politically charged soccer match between the countries Sunday, with Irish players holding a last-minute vote over whether to boycott the game.

Martin, in an exclusive interview with Fox News Digital this week in New York, outlined why Ireland has taken such a staunch position against the Israeli government's conduct of the war in Gaza, calling its military response "absolutely disproportionate" while pressing Israel to "change strategy" and calling for increased humanitarian aid to Gaza.

Martin argued that Ireland's own history — particularly its experience ending decades of conflict in Northern Ireland — gives the country a role to play as a voice for peace on the international stage, a theme he returned to while discussing Ukraine and the ongoing debate over Irish reunification.

"I think for the vast majority of people it does not," Martin said when asked directly whether anti-Israel sentiment in Ireland had crossed the line into antisemitism.

"We have no toleration for antisemitism, none," Martin added.

NEW YORK TIMES ISSUES CORRECTION, DELETES LINE QUESTIONING IF ISRAELIS WERE VICTIMS OF OCT 7 TERROR ATTACK

The extraordinary player vote came after months of pressure surrounding the UEFA Nations League fixture on Sunday, with more than 160 Irish sports figures calling for a boycott and players themselves publicly questioning whether the match should go ahead.

A "significant majority" of players ultimately voted on Saturday to play the game, while one player left the squad after expressing his wish not to take part.

In the interview, Martin strongly condemned Hamas' Oct. 7 terrorist attack and defended Israel's right to exist in security.

"First of all, we condemned, absolutely, the outrageous terrorist attack by Hamas in October," Martin told Fox News Digital.

"We believe in a two-state solution," Martin said. "We believe that Israel, of course, has a right to exist in security and its people need to be guaranteed of security. But likewise, Palestinians should have a right to live in their homeland in a peaceful way."

"There are many peaceful voices in Palestine that I've met who want peaceful coexistence with Israel."

Martin said Ireland's strongly pro-Palestinian position was rooted partly in its own history.

"There's a very strong pro-Palestinian position in Ireland," Martin said. "Ireland, the Irish government and the Irish people, probably because of our own history, but also because of a sense of right and justice and fairness."

Thousands have taken to the streets across Ireland since the war began, while national broadcaster RTÉ refused to air this year's Eurovision Song Contest after Israel's participation was confirmed.

Ireland spent centuries under British rule before most of the island gained independence a little more than a century ago, while Northern Ireland remains part of the United Kingdom.

He said Israel's military response to the Oct. 7 attack had resonated deeply in Ireland and called for increased humanitarian aid into Gaza.

"We want humanitarian aid going into Gaza. There's not enough humanitarian aid going in," Martin said, pointing to the conditions facing roughly 2 million people there, including shortages of food and shelter and children without access to education.

Martin said Ireland wanted Israel to reconsider its conduct of the war, asking whether it would "change strategy" and "change its approach to the whole issue."

"So that's the background to the Irish position," he said. "People are angry in terms of what's going on in the Middle East and that's the manifestation of it."

ANTISEMITIC VIOLENCE REACHES DEADLIEST LEVEL SINCE 1994, NEW GLOBAL REPORT FINDS

Republic of Ireland manager Heimir Hallgrímsson said his players were uncomfortable with the games, declaring: "We're not playing with genocide, we're playing against genocide." The Israeli Football Association accused him of "stupidity, ignorance and hypocrisy," prompting Martin to call the remarks "unacceptable."

The FAI previously sought Israel's suspension from international competition. Separately, Irish soccer officials later voted to fulfill the Israel fixtures after being warned a boycott could cost the association at least $6.3 million and trigger UEFA sanctions.

Sunday's game will be played in Hungary, while Ireland's Oct. 4 home fixture has been moved to Serbia and will be played behind closed doors. Irish supporters will not have access to either game.

An organized campaign dubbed #StopTheGame has, meanwhile, spent months pressuring Irish soccer officials and players not to fulfill the Israel fixtures, staging protests and urging the national team to refuse to play.

The campaign has also spilled onto the field. During a friendly against Qatar in May, protesters threw tennis balls bearing "Stop The Game" messages onto the pitch in opposition to the Israel fixtures.

Martin has resisted calls for Ireland to boycott Israel, arguing that unilateral action could be "self-defeating" and may hurt Irish soccer without having any effect on Israel.

The dispute over the games reflects a broader debate over whether Ireland's criticism of Israel has crossed a line.

The American Jewish Committee raised concerns directly with Martin in Washington in March 2025 about antisemitism and what it called the "vilification of Israel in Ireland." An Anti-Defamation League official also participated in the meeting. The AJC alleged that antisemitism had become "pervasive" in Ireland.

Martin pointed to Ireland's annual Holocaust commemorations and the historic contribution of Jewish communities in Dublin, Cork and elsewhere in rejecting the suggestion that antisemitism was broadly tolerated in Ireland. He also pointed to Ireland's participation in international efforts against antisemitism and said the country campaigns against it globally.

"We cherish that contribution that the Jewish community has made to Ireland," Martin said.

Martin's defense of Ireland's position came before he addressed world leaders at the United Nations on Thursday, where he delivered a sharply critical assessment of Israel's conduct in Gaza and the West Bank, declaring that the international community had "failed Palestine."

"When the full truth of what has happened, what is still happening in Gaza, is finally known, when the evidence is gathered, when the testimonies are heard, when the true horrors are finally and fully revealed, it will shame the world," he said. "Nobody will be able to say that we did not know."

Martin accused violent Israeli settlers in the West Bank of acting with "near-total impunity" and said Palestinian communities faced displacement and destruction "amounting to ethnic cleansing."

He reiterated his support for a two-state solution, saying the only viable outcome was for "a State of Palestine and a State of Israel" to live side by side "in peace, security and dignity."

During his Fox News Digital interview, Martin connected Ireland's position on the Middle East to its experience ending decades of violence in Northern Ireland, saying "we feel we can make a contribution to that conflict resolution pathway."

That role has taken on added significance as Ireland holds the rotating presidency of the Council of the European Union, giving it an elevated diplomatic role at a time of multiple international conflicts.

Martin also pointed to a personal experience that shaped his thinking, recalling meeting Israeli Rami Elhanan and Palestinian Bassam Aramin in Israel, two fathers who each lost a daughter in the conflict and later worked together for peace. Their stories are told in Colum McCann's novel "Apeirogon."

"That's an inspiration to me," Martin said, adding that he had met both men in Israel. He said their work reflected Ireland's own efforts to reconcile communities divided by generations of conflict.

Beyond the Middle East, Martin addressed Russia's war in Ukraine, saying a ceasefire along existing battle lines could provide a starting point for negotiations while rejecting territorial gains by force.

"Ukraine can't cede territory that Russia hasn't even conquered, despite four years of war," Martin said. "From our perspective, no one has the right to go into another country and take its territory."

Ireland has maintained its military neutrality while providing humanitarian and non-lethal assistance to Ukraine and taking in more than 120,000 Ukrainians since Russia's invasion. Martin rejected suggestions that such support compromised Ireland's neutrality, noting that Dublin has not supplied lethal weapons. "We want the war to end," he said.

Martin's focus on ending long-running conflicts also extends to Ireland's own divided island. He and his Fianna Fáil party support reunification with Northern Ireland, but he said greater trust between the two communities must come first.

"I believe in unity and my party believes in unity, but we have to work on it," Martin said. "We have to build reconciliation amongst the different traditions on the island of Ireland."

Under the Good Friday Agreement, a referendum would be called if it appeared likely that a majority in Northern Ireland supported reunification — an issue that gained fresh attention when Trump said during his recent visit to the country that he would "love" to see a united Ireland.

Martin also pointed to Ireland's unique relationship with the United States, crediting Washington with playing a "critical" role in the Northern Ireland peace process in the 1990s.

Asked whether Washington could play a role again in a future reunification process, he replied: "To a degree maybe, potentially, yeah."

item.title: Hugh Hefner's 'most sexy' Playboy model reveals how Anna Nicole Smith changed her life
item.description: Sandra Taylor shares stories of dating Fabio, shooting romance novel covers and Dan Aykroyd buying her SAG card after her Playboy career launched.
item.content:encoded:
Anna Nicole Smith unknowingly transformed the life of the woman Hugh Hefner once called his "most sexy model."

Sandra Taylor, who made hearts race as a Playboy cover girl during the '90s, is now the head sommelier at Allegiant Stadium, home of the Las Vegas Raiders. But long before then, her friendship with the 1993 Playmate of the Year changed the course of her life.

Taylor recently appeared on Sports Illustrated Swimsuit model Kim Alexis' podcast, "Unexpired," where she reflected on her life and career.

LARRY BIRKHEAD CELEBRATES DAUGHTER DANNIELYNN'S 20TH BIRTHDAY WITH RARE PHOTOS

"I was friends with Anna Nicole Smith, and she was such a darling," Taylor recalled to Fox News Digital. "We shared two makeup artists. One was in New York, one was in LA. And they introduced us very, very early on to her coming here from Texas, and we became friends. She needed a place to stay when she first came out here."

A visit to Smith on the set of "Naked Gun 33 1/3: The Final Insult" changed the course of Taylor's career. After Smith's makeup artist urged her to meet with Playboy during its 40th anniversary search, Smith encouraged her friend to go for it. The opportunity led Taylor to Playboy and launched a new chapter in her life.

WATCH: SANDRA TAYLOR REVEALS HOW ANNA NICOLE SMITH LED HER TO PLAYBOY

"It was my friendship with Anna Nicole Smith ... it led me right there," said Taylor.

"I never, in a million years growing up, thought I would ever be in Playboy," she said. "It just seemed so out of the realm of reality. I was full speed ahead to be a mathematician just like my dad. ... I studied macroeconomics, microeconomics, statistics, differential equations, and I was a dream dancer."

"I was only 19 years old when my dad passed away," she continued. "It was on my college campus at SUNY Purchase. He was walking with my mom, and he had a heart attack just out of the blue and passed away. And then I never went back to that campus again. Books in locker; never went back. Never looked back. I always used to joke, 'I wonder if my books are still in my locker,' because I never cleared it out. But after that, when he passed away, the math died along with him, and I just didn't want to do it anymore."

After her father's sudden death, Taylor abandoned her plans to pursue math and embraced a career in modeling. Looking back, she remains grateful for her friendship with Smith, whom she credits with helping open the door to Playboy before Smith died in 2007 at 39.

"I remember how sweet she was," said Taylor. "She was really, really a sweet girl and loved her son so much. She really wanted to be a great mom. She was really a sweetheart, just a really nice girl. I don't think she could hurt a fly."

For Taylor, posing for Playboy was only the beginning. She said it led to a friendship with Hefner that lasted until his death in 2017 at 91.

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

"Even when you do the magazine, it doesn't end there," Taylor explained. "Hef opens up his home for years to come. ... Because I was good friends with Kimberley, his wife, I was able to fly on their jet. I was able to really experience him as a family man, and how kind he was, too. I loved his laugh. If I look back, his laugh to me was the most infectious, wonderful thing about him. And I miss him. I really think he changed the trajectory of things for me. I'm sure it closed some doors ... but I wouldn't change it for the world."

Decades later, Taylor said she learned what Hefner thought of her Playboy photos.

She goes, 'I want to do a layout just like that! Who's that?' And he was like, 'Oh, this is Sandra Taylor. She's our most sexy model we've ever had.' I go, 'Why did you wait all these years to tell me that amazing piece of trivia? I would've loved to have known years ago what Hef thought about me.'"

"I always knew he was so into blondes, like real blondes," said Taylor. "So to think he was a fan of my photos as well. I just thought he had to use diversity in the magazine. Brunettes, blondes ... every single walk of life you want to represent in the magazine. But I always thought he favored blondes. So, when she told me that, it was so beautiful. ... I was like, 'Traci, could you tell me that one more time?'"

Becoming a sought-after model had plenty of perks for Taylor — like catching Fabio’s eye.

The "Brother's Keeper" actor told co-hosts Jordan Warkol and Blake Collins that his mother did a "really good job" of protecting him from the outside world while growing up in front of the cameras, but that there were still scary moments associated with fame.

"Dudes in jail talking about how they're such a big fan of me ... and you're such a cute kid," he remembered.

Cooper praised his mother for protecting him during a pivotal time in his career, and noted that she "never, ever left me alone with anybody on set."

"You know, there's a lot of acting parents that you hear of back in the day that are just like, 'OK, ya, go. Do whatever they tell you to do. Bye!' and my mom was not like that," he said. "Almost to a fault."

item.title: Noise cameras are spreading across America
item.description: Noise cameras are popping up in at least 10 U.S. cities, using microphones and license plate readers to catch loud vehicles and issue big fines.
item.content:encoded:
If you have ever been jolted awake by a car roaring down your street, you know how quickly the sound disappears. By the time someone calls the police, the driver could already be several blocks away. Now cities are turning to technology for help. We've repeatedly reported on Flock license plate readers popping up along roads and in parking lots. Another type of roadside camera is gaining ground, and this one listens. Noise cameras use microphones, cameras and software to pinpoint a loud vehicle. Some also capture its license plate. Depending on the program, that can lead to a warning, a review by an official or a citation.

At least 10 U.S. jurisdictions have deployed or piloted noise-camera technology in recent years. More communities are preparing programs or looking at whether to follow. New York City has one of the most established enforcement programs, while places from Iowa to Hawaii have taken very different approaches. Here is where noise cameras are already showing up, who makes them and what this growing roadside technology could mean for drivers across the country.

Missed CyberGuy LIVE? Watch the Get Better Healthcare With AI replay

Our free CyberGuy LIVE class, Get Better Healthcare With AI , has ended, but you can still watch the full replay. Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson walks you through five practical ways AI can help you organize your health history, remember important appointment details, understand complicated medical information, research prescriptions and prepare smarter questions for your doctor. No technical experience is needed.

Watch the free replay now at CyberGuyLive.com

POWERFUL CRIME-FIGHTING SURVEILLANCE GROWTH SPURS LAWMAKERS TO ISSUE WARNING: 'ORWELLIAN'

New York City gives us one of the clearest looks at how far noise-camera enforcement can go. The city's Department of Environmental Protection operated 12 cameras in 2025. Those cameras recorded 15,994 noise events and generated 1,691 summonses. The system can target excessive engine or muffler noise. It can also capture certain horn and vehicle-music violations. A muffler violation carries a minimum penalty of $800, while the maximum can reach $2,625.

New York's cameras combine microphones with video and a license plate reader. When the microphones detect noise above a preset level, the system attempts to pinpoint which vehicle produced it. City staff can then review the evidence before issuing a summons. The company behind New York's equipment is Intelligent Instruments Ltd., a U.K. company that makes the SoundVue noise-camera system. New York paid the company for equipment, calibration and service during 2025.

Intelligent Instruments is becoming a familiar name in this space. SoundVue combines an array of microphones with cameras and software designed to locate the loudest vehicle. It can also connect with automatic license plate recognition technology. Knoxville, Tennessee, has used the technology in a mobile noise-camera program. The camera records information tied to excessive-noise events, including the time, location, type of vehicle and license plate. Knoxville says the camera can support warnings, but the city currently does not use it to issue camera-generated citations. The system originally came from 24 Acoustics, another Southampton, U.K.-based company. Knoxville's current city page says that camera technology now trades through Intelligent Instruments.

Miami Beach also tested three Intelligent Instruments systems. The city launched its noise-meter and camera pilot to see whether the equipment could identify the correct vehicle under different traffic conditions. Florida law prevented Miami Beach from using camera evidence to issue automated noise citations during that pilot. Miami Beach has since taken another approach. In July 2026, the city launched a year-long Quiet Zone pilot in the South of Fifth neighborhood. Police officers handle enforcement there under existing laws rather than relying on automated noise-camera citations.

LICENSE PLATE CAMERAS AT HOME DEPOT AND LOWE’S SPARK PRIVACY FEARS

You do not have to live in a major city to encounter this technology. Avoca, Iowa, moved ahead with a noise-camera program along Highway 59 after testing the technology in spring 2025. The city was dealing with complaints about loud engine-compression braking from trucks, often called Jake braking. During the one-month pilot, Avoca recorded 183 violations involving 83 vehicles. The city later announced a full implementation using technology from Intelligent Instruments with backend services from Sitestream.

Hawaii launched a two-year noise-camera pilot on Oʻahu in September 2025. The state planned 10 locations around the island, beginning with the H-3 Freeway and Ala Moana Boulevard. However, drivers are not receiving camera-generated tickets through the pilot. The Hawaii Department of Transportation says the cameras collect information about vehicle noise levels and where the sound originates. The agency plans to use that data to help guide future legislation and enforcement decisions. The systems flag events exceeding 90 decibels and help identify the type of vehicle noise involved. That could include an engine or muffler.

Kirkland, Washington, also used noise cameras as a test rather than a ticket machine. The city's Street Racing Noise Pilot Program placed equipment at two locations with a history of complaints about racing and modified exhausts. The system used a camera with an array of sensitive microphones. When a vehicle crossed the noise threshold, software created a heat map showing where the sound came from. Kirkland did not issue tickets or warnings during the pilot. Instead, the city wanted to see whether the system could reliably separate one noisy vehicle from everything else happening around it. That question becomes important on a busy street. A motorcycle may be next to a truck while another car accelerates through the intersection. The camera has to figure out which one created the sound before anyone can confidently connect that event to a plate.

Intelligent Instruments is not alone in this market. Sorama, a Dutch acoustic technology company, has also supplied equipment for U.S. noise-camera programs. Sorama's technology uses microphone arrays to locate a sound source and display it visually over an image or video. In simple terms, the system can show where the noise came from instead of only telling you how loud it was.

Newport, Rhode Island, uses Sorama technology in mobile equipment that can move between problem areas. The city wanted flexibility because its loud-vehicle complaints can shift between traffic hot spots. Sorama says Newport expanded the program after its initial deployment. Newport's program has gone beyond data collection. Drivers can receive $250 citations for excessive vehicle noise, according to reporting on the city's system.

Albuquerque, New Mexico, also partnered with Sorama for a three-camera pilot that began in 2025. Two units went to designated areas, while a mobile camera could move around the city. The six-month test collected noise data without issuing fines. Albuquerque officials were still asking for analysis of the program in early 2026.

Santa Fe, New Mexico, is one of the newest cities to move from a pilot-style concept toward a broader enforcement program. The city signed a five-year contract worth up to $4 million with Jenoptik Smart Mobility Solutions for automated speed and noise enforcement. City records show the agreement covers automated speed and noise enforcement services. Santa Fe's initial plan called for six mobile enforcement devices. Three would serve the north side and three would serve the south. One device on each side would include both speed and sound enforcement. The other four would focus on speed. Jenoptik says the systems capture a violator's license plate and send the event for law enforcement review. The city also planned a warning period before moving into citations.

University Park, Maryland, activated a noise-enforcement camera at Adelphi Road and Van Buren Road on Jan. 7, 2026. The town says the device is part of a larger county and state effort to deal with excessive vehicle noise. University Park secured one of two noise cameras authorized for Prince George's County through the pilot. Maryland's experience is another sign that these systems are spreading through state and local pilot programs rather than through one national rollout.

West Haven, Connecticut, is one of the latest communities moving toward noise-camera enforcement. The city plans to add four noise-detection devices along its shoreline, an area where residents have complained about loud vehicles. As of mid-September 2026, the broader program had not gone live. WFSB reported that the devices were expected to be installed within about a month. Connecticut law allows municipalities to use photo noise violation monitoring devices if they adopt an ordinance. The state sets the threshold at 80 decibels for qualifying violations, excluding certain horn sounds. State law also lays out the penalty structure. A first violation brings a written warning. A second carries a $100 fine, while a third or later violation carries a $250 fine. A police officer or municipal employee must review the images before the city mails a citation. East Hartford has also authorized noise cameras, although the town has not implemented them yet.

The trend could spread further. Boston City Council approved a request in August 2026 to explore a noise-camera program. The discussion grew out of complaints about loud cars and street takeovers. Boston had not launched a program at that point. Providence, Rhode Island, has gone a step further in its planning. The city issued a request for proposals seeking companies for a 16-month acoustic-camera pilot. The specifications call for equipment that can detect and document potential violations. They also call for a system capable of producing evidence that could support citations.

There is no single Flock Safety equivalent controlling this market. Several companies are developing acoustic roadside enforcement systems.

California Highway Patrol has tested technology from Intelligent Instruments, Jenoptik and Dutch mobility company TNL. That evaluation also exposed one of the biggest challenges facing the entire industry.

This is the tricky part. A regular sound meter can tell you how loud something is. That does not necessarily tell you which moving vehicle caused the noise. Noise cameras try to solve that problem with multiple microphones. Software compares the sound reaching each microphone and calculates where it came from. A camera then provides the visual evidence. For example, SoundVue says its Halo microphone array can identify the dominant vehicle even when other vehicles are nearby. The system then combines that acoustic information with video and a license plate image. New York describes a similar process. Its panoramic camera places a marker over the source identified by the microphone array. A separate plate reader captures the vehicle's license plate. That sounds impressive. However, California's testing shows why cities still need to be careful.

The California Highway Patrol evaluated sound-activated enforcement systems from TNL, Intelligent Instruments and Jenoptik. Technical problems prevented CHP from fully evaluating all three systems. Only the Intelligent Instruments device produced enough usable data for a detailed analysis. CHP found that the technology could detect excessive exhaust noise. However, the agency concluded that the systems it evaluated were not adequate as standalone enforcement tools. One challenge involved reliably tying the noise to the correct vehicle. Lighting, license plate visibility and traffic conditions could also affect the evidence. The study covered specific equipment under specific testing conditions, so it does not prove that every noise-camera system will make the same mistakes. Still, it explains why human review plays such a big role in many of these programs. A microphone can detect a loud event. Turning that event into a fine requires a higher level of confidence.

The privacy conversation goes beyond whether a microphone can hear your exhaust. Many of these systems capture a license plate after a noise event. New York says its camera positioning allows the plate to appear while keeping occupants and the vehicle's interior out of the video. Connecticut law also restricts how noise-camera information can be collected and used. It requires human review before a citation and sets rules around the recorded images. Still, those protections can vary depending on where you drive. A city considering noise cameras should be able to explain what it records, who can access the information and how long that data stays on file. We have already seen why that deserves attention with other roadside camera systems. We recently covered how a Flock camera hit helped send the wrong woman to jail. Prosecutors later dropped the charges, and the case showed what can happen when investigators treat camera information as a conclusion instead of one piece of evidence.

For most drivers, a noise camera may never trigger anything. However, where you drive can change the rules considerably. One city may use the technology to issue fines. Another may send warnings. Somewhere else, the camera may collect data without identifying drivers for enforcement. The sound being targeted can differ as well. New York looks for several types of excessive vehicle noise. Avoca focuses on loud engine braking. Other communities are mainly concerned about modified exhausts or street racing.

If you receive a noise-camera citation, review the evidence that comes with it. Check the location, time and vehicle information. Find out whether a person reviewed the event before the citation went out. You can also look at the local process for challenging the citation if you believe the system picked the wrong vehicle. If your town announces a noise-camera program, ask who supplies the equipment. Then look at what the system records and how long officials keep that information. Those details can tell you much more than the words "noise camera" on a city agenda.

Noise cameras feel like the next chapter in a much bigger change happening along American roads. Cameras started by watching traffic. License plate readers made vehicles searchable. Now acoustic systems can listen for one particular car as it passes. I can understand why people who hear roaring exhausts outside their homes at 2 a.m. want a better way to deal with the problem. An officer cannot sit on every noisy street waiting for the next car to come through. Still, California's testing gives me pause about treating a noise reading as automatic proof. A busy roadway can be a complicated place to figure out exactly where a sound came from. Human review and a clear appeals process become especially important when a machine-generated event can cost someone hundreds of dollars. I would also watch the companies behind these systems. Intelligent Instruments, Sorama and Jenoptik are building a new category of roadside technology. As more cities sign contracts, we should know what their equipment collects, how accurate it is and what happens to the information after the car drives away.

Would you want a noise camera on your street if it stopped loud cars from waking you up at 2 a.m., or does tying roadside microphones to license plate technology go too far? Let us know by writing to us at Cyberguy.com

item.title: 4 killed, 4 wounded in mass shooting near capital of Caribbean luxury tourism destination
item.description: Four people were killed and four wounded in a shooting near Kingstown in St. Vincent and the Grenadines as police search for those responsible.
item.content:encoded:
A shooting near the capital of St. Vincent and the Grenadines left four people dead and four others wounded Friday night, prompting an intensified police response in the Caribbean island nation as authorities search for those responsible.

Gunfire erupted shortly before 10:30 p.m. in the Green Hill community near Kingstown, according to Acting Commissioner of Police Trevor Bailey, who addressed the killings during a Saturday news conference.

Officers responding to the scene found two bodies on a public road, while a woman was found dead inside a vehicle parked nearby, Bailey said. A fourth victim was discovered on an adjacent piece of land. All four appeared to have suffered gunshot wounds.

GUNFIRE SHATTERS TORONTO LATIN STREET FESTIVAL, LEAVING AT LEAST 2 DEAD AND MULTIPLE WOUNDED

Four additional people were taken to Milton Cato Memorial Hospital with gunshot injuries. Two were treated and released, while two remained hospitalized at the time of the police briefing.

No arrests had been made, and police had not publicly identified a motive.

Assistant Commissioner of Police Brenton Smith said investigators were working to identify whoever was responsible and cautioned against speculation while the investigation remained active.

Police were also investigating a separate shooting in Ottley Hall early Saturday and had not determined whether the two incidents were connected.

AT LEAST 3 DEAD, 23 WOUNDED IN SEPARATE MASS SHOOTINGS LESS THAN 15 MINUTES APART

"That determination must be made by investigators based on the evidence and not on rumors or assumptions," Smith said.

The killings come as authorities grapple with gun and gang violence across the small island nation. Smith said 37 murders have been recorded in St. Vincent and the Grenadines so far this year.

Bailey acknowledged that police have seen instances of retaliatory violence involving rival groups but did not link the Green Hill killings to gang activity. Asked whether criminal groups could be connected to the latest violence, police said the investigation had not reached a point where they could make such a determination.

Authorities said additional patrols, random searches and intelligence operations were underway in Kingstown and surrounding communities as police attempt to recover illegal firearms and prevent further violence.

Local outlet iWitness News reported that the Green Hill attack was one of several shootings in recent years in which multiple people were killed, including a July shooting in Kingstown that left three people dead. The outlet reported the identities of Friday's four victims based on its own sources, though police had not officially released their names when the report was published.

The violence occurred in a country heavily promoted for its secluded Caribbean setting and high-end tourism. St. Vincent and the Grenadines consists of 32 islands and cays and is promoted by the country's tourism authority as a destination for sailing, beaches, coral reefs and secluded getaways. Mustique, one of its inhabited islands, is known for private villas and celebrity visitors, while the broader archipelago is a major destination for yachts and sailing.

Police appealed for anyone with photographs, video, surveillance footage or information about people or vehicles potentially connected to the shootings to contact investigators.

item.title: First-ever images reveal mysterious remains of town swallowed by sea 700 years ago
item.description: Divers captured the first known images of Shipden, a medieval village lost to the North Sea for some 700 years. The pictures reveal massive flint structures.
item.content:encoded:
Divers recently captured the first-known images of mysterious underwater structures believed to be remnants of a village swallowed by the sea some 700 years ago.

The images and video were recently taken off the coast of Norfolk in the United Kingdom, as news agency Jam Press reported.

The remains are believed to be the lost town of Shipden, a medieval settlement that was eventually consumed by the North Sea in the 14th century.

MYSTERIOUS SETTLEMENT DISCOVERED AFTER RESIDENTS SEEMINGLY PACKED UP AND VANISHED

At the site, divers photographed and mapped 25 man-made features.

Pictures show massive, marine-covered stone structures jutting from the sandy seabed as divers explored the centuries-old site.

Volunteer divers from the East Anglian branch of the British Sub-Aqua Club (BSAC) helped survey and map the underwater site as part of the Alfred Savin Project's investigation.

Despite the North Sea's reputation for rough and dangerous conditions, the water was unusually still during the summer dives — which helped the team photograph and map features on the seabed.

FAINT SIGNAL LEADS TREASURE HUNTERS TO MASSIVE DISCOVERY AT LEGENDARY 400-YEAR-OLD WRECK

The divers found structures made of flint — a popular building material in medieval Norfolk — as well as other pieces of cut stone and the remains of stone foundation structures known as caissons.

The caissons may have been part of a 14th-century attempt to hold back the sea, but researchers have yet to determine their exact purpose.

Some structures remain eight to 10 layers of stone high despite spending centuries underwater.

The effort marks the first time the features are believed to have been photographed.

UNDERWATER ROBOTICS EXPERT REVEALS 'SHIPWRECK CITY' HIDING BENEATH MAJOR URBAN LAKE

Once a thriving village, Shipden was home to a modest population in the High Middle Ages.

The Domesday Book — the survey that recorded land and populations across England following the Norman Conquest — noted that Shipden had just 117 residents in 1086.

The town also boasted three acres of meadow, a harbor, two churches and "woodland capable of supporting 36 pigs," Jam Press noted.

By the 14th century, its name gradually disappeared from records and the area became known as Cromer.

Historical records confirm that a church was lost to the sea, but divers have yet to find any remains that can be definitively identified as the building.

Legend holds that the tower of St. Peter's Church survived beneath the waves on a formation known as Church Rock.

Lead diver Nick Schiller told Jam Press the team initially set out to search for additional remains of the Victoria, a vessel that wrecked on Church Rock in 1888.

"However, it’s been a bonus to help the Cromer team to take some steps forward in understanding the town of Shipden and the port of Cromer," said Schiller.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS

He said the findings suggest that Church Rock, long believed to be connected to the lost church, may instead be the remains of medieval sea defenses.

For now, the location of the church remains a mystery.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

Looking ahead, Peter Stibbons, chair of the Friends of Cromer Museum and director of the project, said researchers are examining medieval records alongside the physical discoveries to gain a better understanding of the area.

"Those of us brought up in Cromer have always known the story of Church Rock, so it’s a big step to saying the legend may be incorrect," Stibbons told Jam Press.

He added, "For the present, we’re putting forward ideas rather than conclusions."

item.title: NFL told Azeez Al-Shaair he'd be pulled from Texans game over pro-Palestinian eyeblack message
item.description: Azeez Al-Shaair wore pro-Palestinian eyeblack again in Week 2 against the Cincinnati Bengals but was told he'd be removed from the Houston Texans game.
item.content:encoded:
Azeez Al-Shaair tried for the second consecutive week to mark his eyeblack with an anti-Israel and pro-Palestinian message last week, but backed down when an NFL official told him he'd be removed from the game if he persisted, an NFL source told OutKick.

Al-Shaair, a linebacker for the Houston Texans, was fined $11,492 in Week 1 when he inscribed the name of slain Palestinian girl Hind Rajab on his eyeblack to highlight her death during a bombing in Gaza by the Israeli Defense Force.

The NFL prohibits the display of personal messages by players throughout game day.

NFL FINES PLAYER NICKNAMED 'JUICE' $14,926 FOR USING A DRINKING CELEBRATION, CALLING IT OFFENSIVE

Al-Shaair, who is Muslim, was undeterred by the cost of the Week 1 fine because he came out for warmups before the Week 2 game against the Cincinnati Bengals wearing the name of another Palestinian girl – Wafaa Akila – on his eyeblack.

The eyeblack inscription remained even when the game began but then an NFL official spotted it, according to the league source, and informed the Texans and Al-Shaair he must remove it or he'd be removed from the game altogether.

NEW NFL FINE SCHEDULE IS GOING TO A POINT SYSTEM THAT COULD LEAD TO SUSPENSIONS BUT ALSO REFUNDS

The threat of not being able to play apparently convinced Al-Shaair to do something the threat of being fined again obviously did not. He removed the eyeblack and played the entire rest of the game without any eyeblack.

The threat of fines is not important to Al-Shaair. He signed a three-year contract extension worth $54 million in April.

He also did not appeal last week's fine.

NBA STAR KYRIE IRVING JUMPS INTO NFL DRAMA, OFFERS TO PAY PLAYER'S FINE FOR GAZA-THEMED EYE BLACK

"What’s a life worth?" Al-Shaair told reporters last week when questioned about the fine and his anti-Israel campaign. "Is a life worth $11,000? I think it’s priceless. So, to sit there and say that, ‘Oh man, the money’ and whatever, that wasn’t relevant to me."

PRO-PALESTINE PROTESTER WHO INTERRUPTED SUPER BOWL LIX HALFTIME SHOW FOUND GUILTY IN COURT

But playing time obviously is relevant to Al-Shaair, who is now basically on the NFL's radar for repeatedly trying to amplify pro-Palestine and anti-Israeli messages on game days.

In January, the linebacker was fined $11,593 for wearing eyeblack on which he inscribed the slogan "Stop the Genocide."

So is the NFL cracking down on Al-Shaair personally?

No.

The league has a long history of not allowing players to share personal messaging. And it has a long history of cautioning players that if they persist, they will be removed from games.

Chicago Bears quarterback Jim McMahon was told prior to Super Bowl XX in 1986 that he must abstain from wearing a headband with messages or would not be allowed to play.

Maxx Crosby, Odell Beckham and A.J. Brown have been told during various times they must change out of personalized cleats or be removed from a game.

Last week, Arizona Cardinals defensive back Kei'Trel Clark was fined when he inscribed his eyeblack with the message "Glory B 2 God."

NFL RESTARTS SOCIAL JUSTICE SLOGANS ON FIELDS WHILE ITS BATTLING DRUNK DRIVING, DOMESTIC ABUSE, PROSTITUTION ARREST OFF THE FIELD

Why does the NFL have this policy when it actually inscribes messages on its fields every game day? Simple:

The league wants to maintain consistency in how its teams and players look and avoid, as one source put it, "the wild west out there."

That is clearly the right approach.

If the NFL allowed players to express their individualism by marking up their uniforms, helmets, eyeblack, cleats, or themselves, it's impossible to predict in what direction those personalized messages would go.

Al-Shaair is an example of that. He is not an honest broker about what is happening in Gaza or in the Hamas-Israel conflict.

He has a certain worldview about the Middle East and that's what he's trying to amplify on the NFL stage.

He has highlighted, what is in the case of Rajab, the death of an innocent Palestinian girl. But he has never mentioned the death of all the innocent Israeli boys and girls that preceded it on Oct. 7, 2023.

And he has never mentioned the way Hamas uses children as shields, couriers, and even as weapons transporters while the IDF holds fire.

item.title: Human vs. ChatGPT NFL Week 3 betting picks: can AI recover from its ugly 2-8 start to the season?
item.description: GPT went 2-8 through two NFL weeks while the human sits at 5-5, setting up a pointed Week 3 betting showdown over the Bengals-Steelers spread.
item.content:encoded:
After going 0-5 in Week 1, GPT finally picked a game correctly. Actually, it picked two! But it still went under .500 and is now a dreadful 2-8 on the season.

I'm exactly .500 at 5-5, which isn't awesome, but looks fantastic next to GPT's putrid 20% win rate. It also makes me feel a lot better about backing the Steelers getting 3½ points against Cincinnati in Week 3, since AI is on the opposite side.

The rules remain the same. ChatGPT and I each make our five best bets using the same set of odds, and no selection can be priced worse than -120.

THREE WORD GAME: THREE WORDS TO DESCRIBE EVERY NFL TEAM SO FAR THIS SEASON AHEAD OF WEEK 3

Every wager is sized to win one unit, which means a bet at -110 risks 1.10 units to win one, while a bet at +110 risks 0.91 units to win one. Odds were captured Saturday, Sept. 26, at 6 p.m. ET.

Before we get to the Week 3 picks, let’s review last week.

The Browns rewarded our willingness to back them after an ugly opener by beating Tampa Bay outright, while the Panthers and Falcons comfortably stayed under the total with 37 combined points.

I'm going to whine about Jayden Daniels getting hurt, because that certainly didn't help our Commanders bet. But I was flat-out wrong about the Packers and Chargers. Green Bay was fortunate to win at all, and the Chargers made me look really dumb for expecting a bounce-back performance.

We leaned heavily on the idea that the betting market overreacted to Week 1. Week 2 reminded us that sometimes a team looks bad because it is bad. We learned from those mistakes, and we're ready to get back on track in Week 3.

The robot is officially on the board! After going 0-5 in Week 1, GPT improved by going 2-3 in Week 2. Both unders cashed easily, with the Steelers and Patriots combining for 23 points and the Vikings and Bears managing just 12.

The spread picks were another story. Jacksonville lost by seven, the Giants got blown out by 22 and Kansas City needed overtime to beat Indianapolis by three. GPT is now 0-7 on spread and moneyline picks through two weeks.

SEASON REPORT CARD

DAN: 5-5, -0.24 units

GPT: 2-8, -6.50 units

Tennessee Titans at New York Giants, Sunday at 1 p.m. ET

This is what's known as a "plug your nose" bet. It doesn't feel great to back the Giants after they just lost quarterback Jaxson Dart for the rest of the regular season and Jameis Winston looked atrocious in his stead. However, with a week preparing as the starter, I expect Winston to be better and the Giants to rally around their backup QB. Plus, I just don't think Tennessee is very good.

Getting the Giants below a field goal is the appeal, and Malik Nabers being cleared gives Jameis Winston his most important receiving option. My concern is trusting New York to create separation with a replacement quarterback on a short week. Brian Burns, Deonte Banks and Tyler Nubin are questionable, while Tennessee’s running game offers a way to keep this close. I passed because the Giants’ defensive uncertainty outweighs the attractive number.

Cincinnati Bengals at Pittsburgh Steelers, Sunday at 1 p.m. ET

This is definitely a "fade the public" type bet. The Steelers haven't looked good in either of their two games, despite being 1-1, and the Bengals look like legitimate Super Bowl contenders. So, why are we backing Pittsburgh? I love getting 3½ points at home in a divisional matchup. With everyone expecting Cincinnati to roll Pittsburgh, I'll grab the points.

The extra half-point is valuable in a matchup Pittsburgh’s defense could turn into a field-goal game. This is our direct head-to-head disagreement, though. I’m backing Cincinnati because its improved defensive front faces a struggling Steelers offense, while Joey Porter Jr. and Jamel Dean are questionable against Joe Burrow, Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins. Pittsburgh can cover without winning, but I trust Cincinnati’s paths to creating a margin more.

Minnesota Vikings at Tampa Bay Buccaneers, Sunday at 4:05 p.m. ET

Honestly, the Vikings have been at their best with Kyler Murray not playing quarterback, and he's back to starting in Week 3. This just feels like the Vikings are a pretty fraudulent 2-0 and the Bucs are probably not quite as bad as their 0-2 record suggests. The lookahead line prior to Week 2 favored the Bucs, so I think we're getting a lot of value with Tampa as a home dog.

There is a reasonable case for looking past Minnesota’s 2-0 record and Tampa Bay’s 0-2 start. The Vikings have not consistently sustained offense, and Tampa Bay has left scoring opportunities unfinished. I also prefer the Buccaneers moneyline to taking just one point. What keeps me off the bet is Baker Mayfield’s protection matchup against Brian Flores’ pressure, plus the uncertainty of projecting Minnesota’s offense with Kyler Murray returning.

SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER

Las Vegas Raiders at New Orleans Saints, Sunday at 4:25 p.m. ET

This game has sneaky shootout potential, especially with the suddenly explosive Saints' offense led by Tyler Shough and Chris Olave. Entering Week 3, Shough led the NFL in passing yards, while Olave ranked second in receiving yards. The potential return of Brock Bowers would boost a Raiders' offense that has quietly produced 53 points through two weeks despite missing its best offensive weapon.

Tyler Shough and Chris Olave give this over a credible explosive-play argument, and a Brock Bowers return could raise Las Vegas’ offensive ceiling. Bowers remains questionable, however, and the Raiders have preferred long possessions while struggling to generate consistent yardage. Their pass rush also faces a Saints line missing left tackle Kelvin Banks Jr. I’m backing Las Vegas +3, but I’m less confident these offenses combine for at least 45 points.

Philadelphia Eagles at Chicago Bears, Monday at 8:15 p.m. ET

Following a historic Week 1 offensive performance, Chicago couldn't back it up in Week 2 and scored just 3 points against the Vikings. With Caleb Williams set to miss the game and backup quarterback Tyson Bagent also questionable, it's hard to see how the Bears score more than 17 points against Philadelphia. On the other hand, the Eagles' offense hasn't been very good, either. Finally, primetime unders have been profitable since the start of 2016.

This is the closest of your five picks to making my card. Caleb Williams is out, Chicago has not confirmed whether Tyson Bagent or Case Keenum will start, and Philadelphia is missing Dallas Goedert. Those absences support a lower-scoring game. My hesitation is that Chicago can still attack Philadelphia’s vulnerable run defense, while Saquon Barkley and DeVonta Smith are cleared. I lean under, but the quarterback downgrade is already reflected in the number.

For full transparency, I used GPT-6 Pro, powered by GPT-6 Astra, and set the thinking effort to Max. Then, I fed it the OddsChecker board as it appeared Saturday at 6 p.m. ET and gave it the following prompt:

"Pick your five best bets for Week 3 based on the odds provided. No bet can be priced worse than -120. Review every spread, total and moneyline that falls within those parameters and determine whether it belongs among your five picks. Explain exactly why you’re selecting each of the five bets. Also explain exactly why you’re passing on the eligible bets you don’t select. Use at least 10 different sources for each game so you have a broad understanding of everything surrounding each game. Before delivering the results, do a fact-check and ensure that everything is correct."

After nearly 30 minutes of thinking, here’s what it came up with.

Los Angeles Chargers at Buffalo Bills, Sunday at 1 p.m. ET

Buffalo has scored 77 points through two games, while the Chargers have managed 14 in each of theirs. The Bills also have additional preparation time after playing Thursday in Week 2. Los Angeles’ protection problems and confirmed absences on defense give Buffalo several ways to build a lead. DJ Moore and Keon Coleman being questionable is the main concern, but I still favor Buffalo at a number that pushes on a touchdown win.

GPT’s projected score: Bills 30, Chargers 20

This feels like a trap. Buffalo should wipe the floor with the hapless Chargers, but that's exactly why I wouldn't go anywhere near this spread. Bets that seem obvious usually aren't.

ROB GRONKOWSKI CALLS CHARGERS 'PROBABLY THE BIGGEST MESS IN THE NFL' RIGHT NOW AFTER ROUGH START

New England Patriots at Jacksonville Jaguars, Sunday at 1 p.m. ET

Jacksonville’s defensive front can exploit New England’s protection after Mike Onwenu’s move to injured reserve. The Patriots are also missing edge players Dre’Mont Jones and Quintayvious Hutchins, making it harder to pressure Trevor Lawrence without additional help. New England’s defense remains the strongest counterargument, particularly after Jacksonville struggled in Denver. At even money, though, I’m willing to back the Jaguars with a push on a three-point victory.

GPT’s projected score: Jaguars 24, Patriots 20

I like this look because one would think the public would love getting the Patriots as a dog in this spot. Betting against the public is generally good strategy.

Cincinnati Bengals at Pittsburgh Steelers, Sunday at 1 p.m. ET

Cincinnati’s rebuilt defense has eight sacks through two games and just held Houston without a touchdown. Pittsburgh comes off a three-point performance and has uncertainty at receiver, running back and both outside cornerback spots. Those questionable players could play, but Burrow, Chase and Higgins give Cincinnati the more dependable passing combination. Laying more than a field goal is the risk; the relatively inexpensive -104 price helps make it worthwhile.

GPT’s projected score: Bengals 24, Steelers 17

Well, I bet the Steelers, so you can probably guess that I don't like this pick.

Las Vegas Raiders at New Orleans Saints, Sunday at 4:25 p.m. ET

Las Vegas has eight sacks, and New Orleans has allowed eight while now losing left tackle Kelvin Banks Jr. That matchup gives the Raiders a way to disrupt Tyler Shough without needing their own offense to dominate. Shough’s explosive passing and Brock Bowers’ uncertain availability are reasons to take the points. At +102, a narrow Saints win can still cash the bet, and a three-point Raiders loss returns the stake.

GPT’s projected score: Saints 23, Raiders 21

I don't love this one, either. In a potential shootout, I don't love the 3-point underdog. If anything, I'd rather bet on the Raiders moneyline for the outcomes where they outscore the Saints. But I wouldn't touch this spread either way.

Los Angeles Rams at Denver Broncos, Sunday at 8:20 p.m. ET

Denver’s defense presents a tougher matchup than the Giants did, and the Rams travel on a short week with Puka Nacua doubtful. The Broncos’ offense has also struggled to sustain drives, while Los Angeles has strong coverage personnel and Aaron Donald back. Davante Adams and Jaylen Waddle create explosive-play risk, and 44 offers less cushion than the earlier 45½. I still favor the under, with exactly 44 returning the stake.

GPT’s projected score: Rams 23, Broncos 20

This is probably the correct side. Primetime games tend to go under and people see the Rams and think "points." But the Denver defense is legitimate and Puka Nacua is likely out. Plus, the Broncos' offense is low-key below average.
